manifest.name: Security
manifest.description: Security posture of the cluster: Pod Security Standards, RBAC, network and secrets checks with a score, accepted risks and Markdown/CSV export.

scan.includeSystemHint: Also scan kube-system, kube-public, kube-node-lease and the cluster's own RBAC objects

overview.title: Security posture
overview.noReportHint: Scan the cluster to see its security posture. A scan only reads the cluster.
overview.columnsLabel: {{category}}: {{critical}} critical, {{high}} high, {{medium}} medium, {{low}} low open findings

findings.title: Security findings
findings.noMatchHint: Change or reset the filters; accepted findings show with the status Accepted or All.

accepted.title: Accepted risks
accepted.emptyHint: Accept a finding from the findings list to record a known, acceptable risk for everyone on this cluster.

accept.title: Accept risk
accept.description: {{title}} on {{resource}} will count as accepted for every user of this cluster, and no longer lowers the score.
accept.reasonHelp: Why the risk is acceptable; shown to everyone and in exports.
accept.expiryHelp: After this the finding counts again.

unaccept.title: Un-accept risk
unaccept.message: {{title}} on {{resource}} will count as an open finding again, for every user of this cluster.

privileged.title: Privileged containers
privileged.message: Containers run privileged, with full access to the node: {{evidence}}
privileged.remediation: Remove securityContext.privileged (and Windows hostProcess) from the containers. Grant the specific capabilities the workload needs instead.

host-namespaces.title: Host namespaces shared
host-namespaces.message: The pod shares the node's namespaces: {{evidence}}
host-namespaces.remediation: Set hostNetwork, hostPID and hostIPC to false (or leave them out). Expose network services through a Service instead of the host network.

host-path.title: hostPath volumes
host-path.message: The pod mounts directories of the node: {{evidence}}
host-path.remediation: Replace hostPath volumes with PersistentVolumeClaims, emptyDir, ConfigMaps or Secrets. If node access is unavoidable, mount the narrowest path read-only.

host-ports.title: Host ports
host-ports.message: Containers bind ports of the node: {{evidence}}
host-ports.remediation: Remove hostPort from the container ports and publish them through a Service (NodePort or LoadBalancer) or an Ingress.

capabilities.title: Capabilities beyond the baseline
capabilities.message: Containers add Linux capabilities outside the baseline allowlist: {{evidence}}
capabilities.remediation: Remove the capabilities from securityContext.capabilities.add; the baseline allows only AUDIT_WRITE, CHOWN, DAC_OVERRIDE, FOWNER, FSETID, KILL, MKNOD, NET_BIND_SERVICE, SETFCAP, SETGID, SETPCAP, SETUID and SYS_CHROOT.

proc-mount.title: Unmasked /proc
proc-mount.message: Containers use a procMount other than Default: {{evidence}}
proc-mount.remediation: Remove securityContext.procMount or set it to Default.

unsafe-sysctls.title: Unsafe sysctls
unsafe-sysctls.message: The pod sets sysctls outside the safe set: {{evidence}}
unsafe-sysctls.remediation: Remove the sysctls from securityContext.sysctls, or configure them on dedicated, tainted nodes instead.

selinux-apparmor.title: SELinux or AppArmor overrides
selinux-apparmor.message: The pod weakens its SELinux or AppArmor confinement: {{evidence}}
selinux-apparmor.remediation: Leave seLinuxOptions.user and role unset, use a container_t-family type, and do not set an Unconfined AppArmor profile.

seccomp-unconfined.title: Unconfined seccomp profile
seccomp-unconfined.message: The pod or its containers explicitly set an Unconfined seccomp profile: {{evidence}}
seccomp-unconfined.remediation: Remove seccompProfile.type: Unconfined from the pod and its containers, and set RuntimeDefault on the pod (or Localhost with a reviewed profile).

privilege-escalation.title: Privilege escalation allowed
privilege-escalation.message: Containers do not set allowPrivilegeEscalation: false: {{evidence}}
privilege-escalation.remediation: Set securityContext.allowPrivilegeEscalation: false on every container.

run-as-non-root.title: Containers may run as root
run-as-non-root.message: Containers are not required to run as a non-root user: {{evidence}}
run-as-non-root.remediation: Set securityContext.runAsNonRoot: true (on the pod or every container) and a non-zero runAsUser; build the image with a non-root USER.

seccomp.title: No seccomp profile
seccomp.message: Containers run without a seccomp profile: {{evidence}}
seccomp.remediation: Set securityContext.seccompProfile.type: RuntimeDefault on the pod (or Localhost with a reviewed profile).

drop-capabilities.title: Capabilities not dropped
drop-capabilities.message: Containers do not drop ALL capabilities, or add back more than NET_BIND_SERVICE: {{evidence}}
drop-capabilities.remediation: Set securityContext.capabilities.drop: ["ALL"] and add back only NET_BIND_SERVICE if the container binds a low port.

volume-types.title: Restricted volume types
volume-types.message: The pod uses volume types the restricted level does not allow: {{evidence}}
volume-types.remediation: Use only configMap, csi, downwardAPI, emptyDir, ephemeral, persistentVolumeClaim, projected and secret volumes; reach other storage through a PersistentVolumeClaim.

resource-requests.title: Missing resource requests
resource-requests.message: Containers do not request CPU or memory: {{evidence}}
resource-requests.remediation: Set resources.requests.cpu and resources.requests.memory so the scheduler can place the pod and evictions treat it fairly.

resource-limits.title: Missing resource limits
resource-limits.message: Containers have no CPU or memory limit: {{evidence}}
resource-limits.remediation: Set resources.limits.memory (and cpu where appropriate), or give the namespace a LimitRange with defaults, so one workload cannot exhaust the node.

probes.title: Missing health probes
probes.message: Containers have no liveness or readiness probe: {{evidence}}
probes.remediation: Add a readinessProbe so traffic only reaches ready pods, and a livenessProbe so a hung container is restarted.

image-tag.title: Mutable image tags
image-tag.message: Containers use the latest tag or no tag: {{evidence}}
image-tag.remediation: Pin images to an immutable version tag, or better to a digest (image@sha256:…), so every pod runs the image that was reviewed.

read-only-root.title: Writable root filesystem
read-only-root.message: Containers can write to their root filesystem: {{evidence}}
read-only-root.remediation: Set securityContext.readOnlyRootFilesystem: true and mount an emptyDir where the application must write.

cluster-admin-binding.title: cluster-admin bindings
cluster-admin-binding.remediation: Bind a role with only the permissions the subjects need; keep cluster-admin for break-glass accounts.

rbac-wildcards.title: Wildcards in roles
rbac-wildcards.message: The role grants rules with wildcards: {{evidence}}
rbac-wildcards.remediation: Replace * in apiGroups, resources and verbs with the explicit groups, resources and verbs the subjects use.

secrets-access.title: Read access to Secrets
secrets-access.remediation: Remove get, list and watch on secrets, or limit the rule to the resourceNames the subjects need; list and watch reveal every Secret's values.

pod-create.title: Pod creation and exec
pod-create.message: The role may create pods or exec into them: {{evidence}}
pod-create.remediation: Grant create on pods (and pods/exec, pods/attach) only to the controllers and people who need it: a new pod can mount any Secret and ServiceAccount of its namespace.

rbac-escalation.title: bind, escalate or impersonate
rbac-escalation.message: The role may escalate its privileges: {{evidence}}
rbac-escalation.remediation: Remove the bind, escalate and impersonate verbs; they let the subjects grant themselves, or act with, permissions they do not hold.

default-service-account.title: Default ServiceAccount in use
default-service-account.message: The namespace's default ServiceAccount should be inert: {{evidence}}
default-service-account.remediation: Set automountServiceAccountToken: false on the default ServiceAccount, do not bind roles to it, and give each workload its own ServiceAccount.

service-account-token.title: Default ServiceAccount token mounted
service-account-token.message: The pod runs as the default ServiceAccount with its API token mounted
service-account-token.remediation: Give the workload its own ServiceAccount, or set automountServiceAccountToken: false on the pod when it does not call the Kubernetes API.

network-policy.title: Namespaces without NetworkPolicy
network-policy.message: The namespace has no NetworkPolicy, so every pod accepts traffic from anywhere
network-policy.remediation: Add a default-deny NetworkPolicy for ingress (and egress) and policies that allow the traffic the workloads need.

secret-env.title: Secrets in environment variables
secret-env.message: Containers read Secrets into environment variables: {{evidence}}
secret-env.remediation: Mount the Secret as a volume and read the files instead: environment variables leak into logs, crash dumps and child processes.

hardcoded-secret.title: Credentials in plain environment values
hardcoded-secret.message: Environment variables that look like credentials have literal values in the manifest: {{evidence}}
hardcoded-secret.remediation: Move the values into a Secret (mounted as a file) or an external secret store; anyone who can read the workload can read them now.

psa-labels.title: No Pod Security admission level
psa-labels.message: Pod Security admission does not enforce a baseline or restricted level: {{evidence}}
psa-labels.remediation: Label the namespace pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce=baseline (or restricted); try it first with the warn and audit labels.

default-namespace.title: Workloads in the default namespace
default-namespace.message: The workload runs in the default namespace
default-namespace.remediation: Move the workload to a namespace of its own, where quotas, policies and RBAC can be scoped to it.
